v.why: Adding a residual where no direct input-output path existed yields large gains (exps 1, 5, 9), far above replacing an existing op.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the direct path loses capacity, giving the smallest or negative gains (exps 2, 6, 10, 14, 18).
In parameter-free pooling cells, an extra skip further dilutes the signal and hurts badly (exps 13-16).
In all-skip cells, adding another identity path degrades accuracy heavily (exps 17-20).
When edge 3 is missing, a skip on edge 4 supplies the residual shortcut and helps much more (exps 65-68, 73-76 vs 61-64, 69-72).
Swapping the only conv out for a skip in pooling-dominated cells removes almost all learnable capacity (exps 79-80).
Deleting edge 0 starves the conv on edge 4, so removal hurts more than when edge 4 is none (exps 42, 45, 54, 56 vs 41, 44, 53, 55).
A conv on edge 5 is more useful when node 2 receives rich conv features from edge 1 (exps 29-36 vs 21-28).
With edge 5 removed, node 2 has no route to the output, so a conv on edge 1 contributes little (exps 85-88, 93-96 vs 81-84, 89-92).
Adding a 3x3 conv yields diminishing returns when the cell already has 3x3 convs, versus big gains in 1x1, skip, or pool cells (exps 81-96 vs 97-100).

raw:
I compared outcomes within the 100 experiments wherever the same edit was applied to parents that differ mainly in the condition edge. I picked the 10 interactions with the clearest evidence:

- **Edge 3 → skip_connect.** This edit helps strongly when edge 3 was empty (exps 1, 5, 9). It hurts or helps little when edge 3 was a convolution (2, 6, 10, 14, 18). It is strongly harmful in all-pooling and all-skip cells (13–20).
- **Edge 4 → skip_connect.** This edit helps when edge 3 is empty, because it supplies the missing shortcut path (65–68 and 73–76, versus 61–64 and 69–72). It is very harmful in avg_pool-dominated cells (79–80).
- **Edge 0 → none.** Removing edge 0 hurts more when edge 4 is a conv. In that case, deleting edge 0 starves a productive path into the output (e4=nor_conv_3x3 rows versus e4=none rows in 41–60).
- **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3.** This edit helps more when edge 1 is already a conv (29–36 versus 21–28).
- **Edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3.** This edit is weaker when edge 5 is none (85–88, 93–96), because node 2 then has no route to the output. It is also much weaker when edge 0 is already nor_conv_3x3 than when the cell lacks 3x3 convs (97–100).
